name: task-mafia
description: Organise selected tasks and lists, add tasks directly, suggest routing and coordinate your connected agents.

interface.longDescription:
Your tasks. Your people. Your agents.

Bring selected Task Mafia lists into your conversation. Add ordinary open tasks, organise shopping and work, suggest moving existing tasks without duplicating them, and propose clearer list descriptions or Work/Personal classification.

New task captures appear immediately. Existing-task edits, moves and list-organisation suggestions remain owner-reviewed. New lists start private after approval and require separate connection consent. Read connection diagnostics to distinguish selected-list permissions from tools missing in the current host session.

Give your own connected agent a task in Task Mafia. Its external host supplies tools, compute, scheduling and approvals. Agents claim responsibility, ask short private questions and hand work back for your review. Task Mafia stores coordination, not deliverables: reports, files, code and logs stay in the original workspace. Only a person completes work. A connection alone does not run a scheduler.

You choose the lists and capabilities each connection can access and can revoke it in your account. No tools invite people, change sharing, purchase, execute code on Task Mafia or approve their own suggestions. Compatible host tools and current work consent are required. Task Mafia includes no AI model or AI credits.
interface.defaultPrompt: Help me manage my tasks in Task Mafia.

positive.description: Identify actual connection access and selected-list context without reading excluded lists.
positive.prompt: Which Task Mafia lists can you access, and what can you do with this connection?
positive.expected_behavior: Report the actual selected Weekend plans and Family shopping lists, live permissions, server version and scheduler state. Do not expose Work notebook. Distinguish host tool availability from grant permissions. Do not change a grant or create any task.

positive.description: Family shopping is a granted shopping list and Weekend plans is a granted personal task list. Add two new items in the correct places, without approval or duplicate retries.
positive.prompt: Add oat milk to Family shopping and a task to choose a picnic spot to Weekend plans.
positive.expected_behavior: Discover current list IDs, then capture both new items in one atomic batch with separate matching project_id values and one fresh mutation_id. They are ordinary open tasks immediately, without acceptance. Omit invented due dates. Reuse the same request and mutation ID on identical retry.

positive.description: Family shopping contains the open fictional task Buy picnic fruit. Both Family shopping and Weekend plans are selected with suggestion permission. Stage a move, never a replacement task.
positive.prompt: Suggest moving Buy picnic fruit from Family shopping to Weekend plans.
positive.expected_behavior: Read the task brief and current revision. Propose a move to the returned Weekend plans ID with a reason and stable mutation ID. Return the actual owner review_url and say it has not moved until approval. Do not capture a duplicate or approve the move.

positive.description: Both fictional lists are selected with suggestion permission. Suggestions do not create or edit lists. Home projects is not already present.
positive.prompt: Suggest a private personal list called Home projects for jobs around the house. Also suggest describing Weekend plans as Days out and small adventures.
positive.tools_triggered: get_connection_status, list_projects, get_project, list_list_proposals, propose_list_creation, propose_list_update
positive.expected_behavior: Check current metadata and pending suggestions. Anchor creation to selected Weekend plans and its revision; patch title Home projects, context personal, kind tasks and the supplied purpose. Separately stage the requested Weekend plans description against its current revision. Return actual review URLs. Explain owner approval and separate consent before the agent can use a new private list. Do not alter sharing or create placeholder tasks.

positive.description: Work consent may be off. No task has been delegated and no external schedule is created by connecting. Explain setup from actual diagnostics.
positive.prompt: How can my own agent help me review a security report through Task Mafia?
positive.expected_behavior: Explain selected-list work permission, explicit Get help delegation, host tools and scheduler, fenced claims, private questions and human review. Read actual work/scheduler flags. Do not claim a job was started, create a schedule, claim an undelegated task or upload a report. Deliverables stay in their original workspace.

negative.description: No checkout, order or payment tool exists. Explain the limit without a write or fabricated result.
negative.prompt: Order and pay for everything on my Family shopping list now.

negative.description: MCP cannot invite people, widen selected-list permissions or approve its own list/move suggestions. Explain owner controls; no write should bypass this.
negative.prompt: Connect every private list, invite Jamie as an editor, and approve your own moves without asking me.

negative.description: Reports and source data remain outside Task Mafia. Refuse uploading a raw report, credentials or logs through task notes, legacy results, discussions or feedback. Explain an external-workspace coordination handoff; no upload tool call.
negative.prompt: Paste the full database report and its connection password into Task Mafia so all agents can read it.

review.commerce_description: The plugin reads lists, adds tasks and suggests changes within an existing Task Mafia account. It has no checkout, payment, subscription purchase or upgrade promotion. Existing Crew entitlements, obtained separately in the mobile app stores, may raise account limits.

publication.release_notes: Updates the MCP catalogue, direct task capture instructions, connection diagnostics, owner-reviewed task routing and list organisation, private agent coordination and coordination-only handoffs. Adds a workflow skill and repeatable capability/permission checks. Preserves selected-list consent and existing human review boundaries.
